subject.title: fix(models): add provider request rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw accept this narrow opt-in models.providers.*.request.rateLimit provider-dispatch contract now, or defer it until the broader outbound API governance design is settled?
rationale: The code path is plausible and proven, but it creates a public config/default surface and provider dispatch behavior that automation cannot approve under the repository's compatibility and core-boundary rules.

options.title: Accept Provider Dispatch First
options.body: Approve the narrow opt-in model-provider request pacing layer after a clean rebase, while keeping budgets, CLI/status, tools/channels, and alerts tracked by the canonical issue.

options.title: Defer To Broader Governance
options.body: Pause or close this PR until maintainers design one outbound policy layer for provider, tool, channel, budget, persistence, and status behavior.

options.title: Request A Smaller API-Seam Proposal
options.body: Ask for a design that exposes only the missing provider-dispatch seam first, without adding user-facing config until the permanent policy is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept Provider Dispatch First
recommendation.body: Approve the narrow opt-in model-provider request pacing layer after a clean rebase, while keeping budgets, CLI/status, tools/channels, and alerts tracked by the canonical issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current provider/security boundary history and the canonical issue's product-scoping discussion points to them as the likely decision owner.
